advances: Conditional on an actual common finite menu, proper endpoint traces, a global affine envelope, and a strict pointed cover at finite buffer.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For any cap in the menu, the two-source buffered base-tilt quota applies. Its left side is positive by the proper source traces. Hence some positive-coarea outside support is strictly beyond the source interval. For a fixed cap there is at most one outside-supporting positive fiber on either side: if $L_1<L_2<a$ were two on the left, interpolate a point on the plane at $L_1$ with a strictly captured point at source $a$ to give strictly captured mass-side incidence at $L_2$, contradicting that outside support. Reflection gives the other side.

For fixed $\xi\in D$, the graph $z\mapsto (z,y(z)+\ell(z)\xi)$ is affine. Its membership set in $C$ is an interval containing $[a,b]$, so the pointed fibers are nested outward on either side. If every cap had a right outside support at a positive sampled base, the last positive sampled fiber would be in every closed complementary pointed cap. The strict weighted sum excludes this. Thus one cap has no right outside support, and the quota gives its unique positive-coarea left outside facet. Reversing the base gives a cap with the opposite incidence. After a reversal if necessary take $\ell$ nondecreasing and choose the former cap, with unique outside facet at $L<a$ of coarea $A_L>0$.

The pointed section of $D$ for this cap has some positive coarea $s_D$ using the same continuous normal divisor as in the quota. The proper section at $b$ has coarea $\ell(b)^{d-1}s_D$; the outside facet at $L$ has coarea at most $\ell(L)^{d-1}s_D$. In each intermediate fiber interpolate a point on the plane at $L$ with a strictly captured point at $b$, and a strictly excluded point at $L$ with one at $b$. These give points on both sides. The intermediate fibers are full-dimensional by interpolation of positive fibers. Hence all integer fibers at $L+1,\ldots,b$ have proper sections. For $d\ge2$, affine translation of the cutting planes aligns these sections in one $(d-1)$-space and preserves their convex combinations. Brunn–Minkowski for that dimension, with $\theta=(z-L)/(b-L)$, gives
$
S_z^{1/(d-1)}\ge (1-\theta)A_L^{1/(d-1)}+\theta S_b^{1/(d-1)}
\ge A_L^{1/(d-1)}\ell(z)/\ell(L).
$
The common normal divisor cancels, and monotonicity gives $S_z\ge A_L$. For $d=1$ all these sections and the outside endpoint have equal counting coarea directly.

With $m=b-a\ge1$ and $h=b-L>m$, drop the nonnegative inside penalty from the quota. The $h$ proper sections give $mhA_L\le (a-L)A_L=(h-m)A_L$, impossible for positive integer $m$. This proves exclusion under the stated affine envelope and strict common menu.
statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with mixed measure summing $d$-volumes of its positive integer fibers $K_z$. Suppose $y(z)$ is affine, $\ell(z)>0$ is affine on the base projection, $0\in\operatorname{int}D$ for a convex $d$-body $D$, and $K_z\subseteq y(z)+\ell(z)D$ at all real bases, with equality for $z\in[a,b]$ for distinct integers $a<b$. There is no finite menu of actual nonvertical buffered caps, each proper at both source fibers and minimizing at both source marks $(a,y(a)),(b,y(b))$ for buffers unchanged under pure base tilt, whose margins in $\xi=(x-y(z))/\ell(z)$ are $u_j\cdot \xi+c_j$ and satisfy $\sum_j\rho_j(u_j\cdot\xi+c_j)>0$ on $D$ for positive weights of sum one.
title: A strict common buffered menu cannot span two homothetic sources
